findings.title: Protected page served from browser cache after logout
findings.detail: Normal navigation to the protected page after logout still showed private content, but a cache-busting request was correctly blocked by the server. The exposure comes from the browser cache, not from the server re-serving private data — still a real exposure for anyone using the same browser.
findings.evidence: GET http://localhost:4001/profile -> 200 after logout, marker present (cached); no-store re-check -> 0 without marker
findings.recommendation: Send Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private on all authenticated responses so the browser never stores them.

findings.title: Protected page allows caching
findings.detail: The protected response allows caching (Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600). Private pages should never be cacheable.
findings.recommendation: Send Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private on all authenticated responses.

notes: Credentials were session-only and were not stored with this run.
